en: <t1>The commit message is a typed value of the executable, with one grammar.</t1> <t2/> is total and never fails; the changelog and the judge read the same parse and disagree only about what to do with a header that is not conventional. For the changelog that is not a failure — a commit nobody spelled conventionally still happened, and a changelog that dropped it would lie about what the release contains. For the judge it is one finding, <t3/>, and its consequences are deliberately not reported as findings of their own: somebody fixing <t4/> does not also need to be told its scope is unknown. There is no second regular expression in a hook, a gate or a script.
cs: <t1>Zpráva commitu je typovaná hodnota spustitelného souboru s jednou gramatikou.</t1> <t2/> je totální a nikdy neselže; changelog a soudce čtou stejný parse a liší se jen v tom, co s hlavičkou, která není conventional. Pro changelog to není selhání — commit, který nikdo nenapsal conventional, se přesto stal, a changelog, který by jej vynechal, by lhal o tom, co release obsahuje.
